lines.japanese: 目覚めると、時計はアラームの一回目に設定した時間だった。
lines.english: When I woke, the clock showed the time I had set for the first alarm.

lines.japanese: 最近は、ここ何年かの朝の淀みが嘘みたいに頭が軽い。
lines.english: Lately, my head felt so light and clear that the murky mornings of the past several years seemed like a lie.

lines.japanese: 僕はもともと朝が得意な方じゃない。授業中でも常に眠たげで、それを一通りの教科の担当から注意された。
lines.english: I had never been much good at mornings. I looked half-asleep even in class, and had been warned about it by teachers in just about every subject.

lines.japanese: 最近は何でも病名と結びつけて、例えば睡眠時無呼吸症候群だから眠くなりやすい、なんて診察も受けずに騒ぐ風潮があるけど、僕の場合はなんてことはない、単に眠いだけだ。
lines.english: These days, people wanted to tie everything to some diagnosis. They would make a fuss about how sleep apnea made them drowsy, for instance, without ever seeing a doctor. My case was nothing so elaborate. I was simply sleepy.

lines.japanese: それがここ一、二週間は、今までの生活が嘘みたいに世界がクリアに見える。何だろう、特に生活の中で意識して変えた点はないんだけどな。
lines.english: And yet, for the past week or two, the world had looked so clear that my life before it seemed unreal. What was it? I hadn't consciously changed anything about the way I lived.

lines.japanese: やっぱり、あれかな。渡来さんの体から出てる新陳代謝をよくする成分に触れる機会が多いからなのかな。
lines.english: Maybe it really was that. Maybe all this contact with whatever metabolism-boosting substance Watarai's body gave off was doing me good.

lines.japanese: 僕は二度目のアラームが鳴る前に目覚ましのスイッチをオフにして、ふとんから飛びおきた。
lines.english: I switched off the alarm before it could ring a second time and sprang out of bed.

lines.japanese: 「んー」
lines.english: “Mmm.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: ちょっと会話のネタになるようなものを探してみたけど、やっぱり今日も思いつかなかった。朝食の海苔を口に運びながらテレビをぼうっと見つめる。
lines.english: I hunted around for something to talk about, but once again, nothing came to me. I lifted a sheet of seaweed from my breakfast to my mouth and stared blankly at the television.

lines.japanese: 「今日は柳木原の花水木通りに来ています。もう街の彩りはクリスマス一色ですね」
lines.english: “Today we're on Hanamizuki Street in Yanagihara. The whole city is already decked out in the colors of Christmas.”

lines.japanese: 「アパレル界の市場調査によれば、今年の２０代女性が選ぶプレゼントの一番人気は腕時計とのことで……」
lines.english: “According to market research from the fashion industry, the most popular gift chosen by women in their twenties this year is a wristwatch...”

lines.japanese: テレビには朝の花水木通りが映っていた。足立アナの背後に、金や赤の派手な装いで飾られた街並みが見える。
lines.english: The television showed Hanamizuki Street in the morning. Behind the reporter, Adachi, the town glittered in gaudy gold and red.

lines.japanese: その途中に、何度か朝食でお世話になったパン屋さんが映っていた。僕はいい話のネタを見つけて、小鳩に向きなおる。
lines.english: For a moment, the report showed the bakery that had furnished our breakfast several times. Glad to have found something to talk about, I turned to Kobato.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、いま映ったパン屋さんって、小鳩が何回か買ってきてくれたお店だよね」
lines.english: “That bakery they just showed—isn't that the one you've bought breakfast from a few times?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はテレビに見入ってたらしく、驚いたように僕の正面に顔を戻した。
lines.english: She must have been absorbed in the television, because she turned back to face me with a start.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いま知ってるパン屋さんが映ったから」
lines.english: “Oh. They just showed a bakery I recognized.”

lines.japanese: 「え、どれどれ」
lines.english: “Huh? Where?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、もう映ってない」
lines.english: “Mmm... It's gone now.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: どうして僕はこう、タイミングが悪いんだろう。小鳩の気の乗らない返事に言葉を返すことも出来ず、玉子焼きに箸を伸ばした。
lines.english: Why was my timing always so bad? Unable to think of any answer to Kobato's listless response, I reached for the rolled omelet.

lines.japanese: でも、小鳩がテレビに見入ってるなんて珍しいな。何を考えてるんだろう。
lines.english: Still, it was unusual to see Kobato so absorbed in the television. What was on her mind?

lines.japanese: 彼女の真似をしてしばらくテレビを見続けたけど、とくに目新しい話題が出たわけでもないみたいだ。毎朝見かける女子アナが、一流ブランドの新製品だとかいう高級ネックレス紹介しているだけだ。
lines.english: I followed her example and watched for a while, but nothing particularly new seemed to come up. The familiar morning announcer was merely showing off an expensive necklace, supposedly the latest thing from some top luxury brand.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩はああいうの欲しい？」
lines.english: “Would you like something like that, Kobato?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん」
lines.english: “No.”
“Ha ha...”

lines.japanese: 彼女からの返事はぶつ切りの相槌。僕はテレビを見るのも諦めて食事に集中した。
lines.english: Her replies came back in clipped little fragments. I gave up on the television and concentrated on breakfast.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、なんて素敵な時計なんでしょう。こんな物を贈られたら、一生付いていきたいなんて思っちゃいますよね」
lines.english: “My, what a lovely watch. If someone gave me one of these, I might just want to follow them for the rest of my life.”

lines.japanese: 「最近では、誕生日よりも、クリスマスプレゼントに力を入れる方が多いようです。私も素敵な聖夜を過ごしたいものです」
lines.english: “Recently, it seems more people are going all out for Christmas presents than for birthday gifts. I hope I get to spend a lovely Christmas Eve myself.”

lines.japanese: 女性アナウンサーのこれみよがしなため息と共に、玉子焼きを口に運ぼうとした僕の手が止まる。
lines.english: The female announcer gave an ostentatious sigh. My hand stopped halfway to my mouth, omelet poised between the chopsticks.
“Oh! The twenty-fourth!”

lines.japanese: 足立アナのおかげで大事なことを思いだした。いや、忘れてたわけじゃない。まだまだ先だと思ってたんだ。
lines.english: Thanks to Adachi, I had remembered something important. It wasn’t that I had forgotten. I had simply thought it was much farther away.

lines.japanese: １２月２４日。それは僕にとって、神様の誕生前夜祭よりも大事な──
lines.english: December twenty-fourth. For me, it marked something more important than the eve of God's birth—

lines.japanese: 「──小鳩の誕生日だよ！」
lines.english: “—your birthday, Kobato!”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yeah.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はゆっくり頷いた。ちょっと気遅れしてる。僕は声のトーンを落としたけれど、妹の健やかな成長という慶びは抑えきれなかった。
lines.english: Kobato nodded slowly, looking a little overwhelmed. I lowered my voice, but I could not contain my joy at seeing my little sister grow up healthy.

lines.japanese: 「そっか、誕生日だ」
lines.english: “That's right. Your birthday.”
“Mm. Yeah...”

lines.japanese: 誕生日ぐらいで大袈裟な、って思われてるかもしれない。でもいいんだ。小鳩ぐらいの歳なら、家族の情を鬱陶しく思いはじめるころだ。むしろ正常な反応に違いない。
lines.english: Maybe she thought I was making far too much of a birthday. That was fine. At Kobato's age, a child was bound to start finding family affection irritating. If anything, her reaction had to be perfectly normal.

lines.japanese: 「何か予定はあるの？」
lines.english: “Do you have any plans?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、べつに」
lines.english: “Mmm. Not really.”

lines.japanese: ふるふると首を横に振る。
lines.english: She softly shook her head.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、どこか出かけようか。クリスマスパーティーも兼ねてさ」
lines.english: “Then why don’t we go somewhere? We can make a Christmas party of it too.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうして？」
lines.english: “W-why?”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: ちょっと考えてみた。よその家でも、兄妹ふたりでクリスマスパーティーなんてやらないのかもしれない。
lines.english: I gave it some thought. Maybe brothers and sisters in other families didn't throw Christmas parties with only the two of them.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、たまには一緒に出かけるのもいいかなって思ったんだけど」
lines.english: “Mmm... I just thought it might be nice for us to go out together once in a while.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は一度大きくうなずいてから、食事を再開させた。
lines.english: Kobato gave one emphatic nod, then went back to eating.

lines.japanese: 「お、お兄ちゃんにあげる」
lines.english: “I-it’s for you, big brother.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 彼女の箸が玉子焼きをつまんで、それを僕の皿の上に落とした。もしかして誕生日のお祝いをすることを喜んでくれたんだろうか。
lines.english: Her chopsticks picked up a piece of omelet and dropped it onto my plate. Could she actually be pleased that I wanted to celebrate her birthday?

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「うんっ」
lines.english: “Mm!”

lines.japanese: お礼を言いながら、妹と毎日会話するという残務処理の一つを思いだす。
lines.english: As I thanked her, I remembered one item of my Unfinished Business: talk with my sister every day.

lines.japanese: 意識して始めようとした会話は失敗したけど、自然と思いだしたことに彼女は喜んでくれた。だったら、無理に兄妹の会話を作る必要はあるんだろうか。
lines.english: The conversation I had deliberately tried to start had failed, but something that came to me naturally had made her happy. In that case, was there any need to force conversation between us?

lines.japanese: 元々は、妹と仲良くすることが目的だった気がする。今だって充分じゃないか。
lines.english: I seemed to remember that the point had been to grow closer to my sister in the first place. Weren’t we close enough already?

lines.japanese: 僕は食事が終わったら、残務処理“５：妹と毎日会話をする”に済みマークを付けることにした。
lines.english: Once breakfast was over, I decided, I would put a DONE mark beside Unfinished Business No. 5: ‘Talk with my sister every day.’

lines.japanese: プレゼントは何を用意しようかなあ、なんて考えながら。
lines.english: All the while, I wondered what I ought to get her for a present.

lines.japanese: 今朝は渡来さんを見かけないなあ、なんて考えながら歩いていたら、いつの間にか昇降口だった。
lines.english: I had been walking along, wondering why I hadn't seen Watarai that morning, when I suddenly found myself at the school entrance.

lines.japanese: 出来れば教室みたいにひとが多い場所じゃなくて、一緒に登校しながら話でも出来ればいいなと思っていたけど仕方ない。
lines.english: I had hoped I could talk to her on the walk to school, somewhere less crowded than the classroom, but it couldn't be helped.

lines.japanese: 登校できれば……。
lines.english: If only we could walk to school together...

lines.japanese: あの渡来明日香と一緒に登校？　な、なにを大それたことを考えてるんだろう。
lines.english: Walk to school with Asuka Watarai? Wh-what outrageous thing was I imagining?

lines.japanese: 「羽田君」
lines.english: “Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 朝の時間を早足に歩いていたら、生徒たちが押しよせるシンデレラ階段で肩を叩かれた。
lines.english: As I hurried through the morning crowd, someone tapped my shoulder on the Cinderella Stairs, where students were pouring upward.

lines.japanese: 「あ、おはようございます」
lines.english: “Oh. Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 担任の女性教諭だった。いつも外から覗くように僕を見ていた冷たい瞳が、今日は年齢相応の穏やかな色を浮かべている。
lines.english: It was my homeroom teacher. The cold eyes that usually seemed to peer in at me from somewhere outside were softened today by a warmth more natural to a woman her age.

lines.japanese: 「卒文の製作を頑張ってるみたいですね」
lines.english: “I hear you've been working hard on the graduation anthology.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい……ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes... Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 一瞬なんのことか分からなかった。今まで何も聞かれなかったから、どこまで進んでいるかなんて、先生は知らないものだと思ってた。
lines.english: For a moment, I had no idea what she meant. She had never asked about it before, so I assumed she knew nothing about how far we had gotten.

lines.japanese: 「みんなが協力してくれるから、順調に進んでます」
lines.english: “Everyone's been helping, so we're making good progress.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか、針生君も協力してくれてますか」
lines.english: “I see. Has Hariu been helping too?”

lines.japanese: 「え、針生さんですか？　はい、手が早いので、とても助かっていますよ」
lines.english: “Hariu? Yes. He works fast, so he's been a tremendous help.”

lines.japanese: 「それはよかった。羽田君、これからも頑張りなさい」
lines.english: “I'm glad to hear it. Keep up the good work, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes, ma'am.”

lines.japanese: 先生はにこにこ笑っていた。だから、僕もつられてにこにこと笑った。
lines.english: The teacher smiled brightly at me. Before long, I was smiling brightly back.

lines.japanese: きっと先生も僕たちの卒業文集を楽しみにしてくれているんだろう。それは、とても嬉しいことだと思った。
lines.english: She must have been looking forward to our graduation anthology too. That made me very happy.

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: 先生に話しかけられている間に、渡来さんが登校してきたみたいだ。僕には気がついてないみたいで、いつかのように、出来すぎた綺麗な脚を交差させながら、一段ずつ上っていく。
lines.english: Watarai seemed to have arrived while I was talking to the teacher. She hadn't noticed me. As she had once before, she climbed one step at a time, crossing those impossibly perfect legs with every step.

lines.japanese: 体調はもうよくなったのかな。僕は歩幅を大きくして、一段飛ばしで階段を上がりながら、その背中を追いかけた。もちろん、下を向きながら。
lines.english: Was she feeling better? I lengthened my stride and bounded up two steps at a time after her—with my eyes lowered, of course.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、渡来さん」
lines.english: “Good morning, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 昨日は体育会系で失敗したので、今日は無難な挨拶にしておいた。とは言っても僕の声はくぐもりやすいので、腹から声を出したつもりだ。
lines.english: Yesterday's sporty greeting had been a failure, so today I kept it safe. My voice tended to come out muffled, though, so I made a point of speaking from the diaphragm.

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Mmm.”

lines.japanese: 今日も渡来さんの最初の返事は挨拶ではなく、なにかの感嘆詞だった。英語に訳したときはどの単語に該当するのか僕にはちょっと分からない。
lines.english: Once again, Watarai’s first response was not a greeting but some kind of interjection. I wasn’t quite sure which English word it ought to become in translation.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 僕に向かって振りかえったときの表情も、昨日の焼き直しみたいな笑顔だった。でも、笑顔のレベルが高いから、焼き直しなんて言ったら失礼か。
lines.english: When she turned toward me, her expression was almost a rerun of yesterday's smile. But her smiles were much too good to call one a mere rerun.

lines.japanese: 「もう体調はいいの？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling better?”

lines.japanese: 「体調？」
lines.english: “Feeling better?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は笑顔のまま、次の言葉を発さなかった。そのまま、数秒の時間が流れる。
lines.english: She kept smiling, but said nothing more. Several seconds passed.

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、大丈夫。もうばっちりよくなった」
lines.english: “Oh. Yeah, I’m fine. Perfectly fine now.”

lines.japanese: そして顔を少しだけ傾けてオッケーのサイン。
lines.english: Then she tilted her head slightly and gave me an okay sign.

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。じゃあ、今日の放課後は作業に参加してもらっても大丈夫かな。さっき、恩田先生にも頑張れって言われたんだ」
lines.english: “I see. Then will you be able to help us after school today? Ms. Onda just told me to keep up the good work.”

lines.japanese: 「放課後？」
lines.english: “After school?”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「あーあーあー、ごめん、駄目駄目、体調駄目。なんかこう、世界中に青い靄がかかってる感じ。痛い痛い、頭痛が痛い」
lines.english: “Ah, ah, ah—sorry. No, no, I'm sick. Very sick. It's like the whole world's covered in a blue haze. Ow, ow—my headache aches.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええっ、それって大変なんじゃないの。全然ばっちりじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Wh-what? That sounds serious. You're not completely better at all.”

lines.japanese: 「おれたち、昨日ずっと心配してたんだよ。駄目じゃん、体調悪いならそう言ってよ」
lines.english: “We were worried about you all day yesterday. If you're sick, you have to tell us.”

lines.japanese: 「心配？」
lines.english: “Worried?”

lines.japanese: 「え、だって、渡来さんが体調悪くて帰ったって聞いたから……」
lines.english: “Well, yes. We heard you'd gone home because you weren't feeling well...”

lines.japanese: それまで表情を崩さなかった渡来さんの眉が、一瞬だけぴくりと下がった。
lines.english: For just an instant, Watarai's brows twitched downward beneath her otherwise unbroken expression.

lines.japanese: 「そっか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、分かった。じゃあ体調悪いからもう行くね」
lines.english: “Mm, got it. Well, I'm sick, so I'll be going now.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は身を翻して教室へと向かってしまった。そんなに辛いのかな。見た感じはすごく元気そうだけど。
lines.english: She wheeled around and headed for the classroom. Could she really be feeling that awful? She looked perfectly healthy.

lines.japanese: だったら相談してくれてもいいのに……いつもの渡来さんらしくない。
lines.english: She could at least have talked to me about it... This wasn't like the usual Watarai.

lines.japanese: あれ？　いつもの渡来さんってどんなだっけ？
lines.english: Wait. What was the usual Watarai like?

lines.japanese: もしかして僕、避けられてる？
lines.english: Could she be avoiding me?

lines.japanese: そんな考えがよぎったけど、心当たりがないので、すぐに打ちけした。きっと体調が悪くて、誰とも話す元気がないんだろう。そう、それだ。
lines.english: The thought crossed my mind, but I had no idea why she would, so I dismissed it at once. She must have been too sick to summon the energy to speak to anyone. Yes. That had to be it.

lines.japanese: 教室に入ろうとしたら渡来さんが友人と廊下に出てきたけど、そのあとを目で追う気にはなれなかった。
lines.english: As I was about to enter the classroom, Watarai came out into the corridor with one of her friends. I couldn't bring myself to follow her with my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっといいか」
lines.english: “Got a minute?”

lines.japanese: 昼休みに一人で学食で買ってきたパンを咥えていたら、針生さんに声をかけられた。教室の視線が集まるのが分かる。
lines.english: At lunch, while I sat alone with a cafeteria sandwich between my teeth, Hariu spoke to me. I could feel the eyes of the classroom gather upon us.

lines.japanese: 針生さんはただでさえみんなの視線を集めやすいひとだ。でも昨日から何度か休み時間に僕と話しているから、すぐにみんなの興味は他に移った。
lines.english: Hariu drew everyone's gaze at the best of times. But he had spoken to me during several breaks since yesterday, and the class soon found something else to be interested in.

lines.japanese: 「はい。いいですよ」
lines.english: “Yes. Of course.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは僕の一つ前の椅子を引き寄せてどかりと腰を下ろした。その手には、小鳩が朝食に何度か買ってきてくれた、花水木通りにあるパン屋さんの袋が握られている。
lines.english: Hariu dragged over the chair in front of mine and dropped heavily into it. In one hand he held a bag from the bakery on Hanamizuki Street where Kobato had bought breakfast several times.

lines.japanese: 「栗山から」
lines.english: “From Kuriyama.”

lines.japanese: そう言って、針生さんは僕にＣＤを一枚押しつけてきた。これは、御影クリヤの新曲……？
lines.english: With that, Hariu pressed a CD upon me. Was this... a new song by Mikage KuRiYa?

lines.japanese: 「あの、栗山さんって御影クリヤのファンなんですか」
lines.english: “Um... Is Kuriyama a fan of Mikage KuRiYa?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　ああまあ、ある意味そうだなァ」
lines.english: “Hm? Yeah. In a manner of speaking.”

lines.japanese: 「このＣＤはどうしておれに？」
lines.english: “Why did Kuriyama want me to have this CD?”

lines.japanese: 「昨日よろしく伝えたら、余ってるからっつって渡された。俺もそんなモンいらねえし」
lines.english: “I passed along your regards yesterday. Kuriyama said there were extras and handed me one. I don’t want the thing.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか。じゃあ、ありがとうございます……」
lines.english: “I see. Then... thank you.”

lines.japanese: そのＣＤは鞄の中に入れておいた。御影クリヤの曲は別に好きじゃないけど、受けとらないのも失礼だろう。
lines.english: I put the CD in my bag. I didn't particularly care for Mikage KuRiYa's songs, but it would have been rude to refuse it.

lines.japanese: 「で、栗山から聞いたんだけど、羽田おまえ、エロゲーって詳しくないか」
lines.english: “Kuriyama told me something. Haneda, you know your way around adult games, don’t you?”

lines.japanese: 僕は口に入れたカツサンドを喉に詰まらせるところだった。何かの冗談かと思って針生さんの顔を見たら、いつもの鋭さをもった目が僕を正面から見据えている。
lines.english: I nearly choked on the cutlet sandwich in my mouth. Thinking it must be a joke, I looked at Hariu, only to find his usual sharp gaze fixed squarely upon me.

lines.japanese: 「近年のシーンを知るには見過ごせない要素らしいんだ」
lines.english: “Apparently it’s an element you can’t afford to overlook if you want to understand the contemporary scene.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どこのシーンの話ですか。知りませんよそんなの、おれはそういうのやったことありませんから」
lines.english: “Wh-what scene are we talking about? I don't know anything about that. I've never played those games in my life.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、おまえなら深い部分とやらを知ってるんじゃないかと思ったんだけどなァ」
lines.english: “Really? I thought you might know about these so-called depths.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはパン屋さんの袋から、サンドイッチを取りだした。ハムと野菜だけのシンプルなサンドイッチは、もちもちしたパンによく合うだろう。ちょっとうらやましかった。
lines.english: Hariu took a sandwich from the bakery bag. The simple filling of ham and vegetables must have gone beautifully with the soft, springy bread. I was a little jealous.

lines.japanese: 「ま、まあ、知らないこともないんですけど、放課後にお願いします」
lines.english: “W-well, I wouldn't say I know nothing, but could we please talk about it after school?”

lines.japanese: 「そう、まァ、おまえがそう言うなら仕方ない。それじゃあ、昨日の話の続きからするか」
lines.english: “Yeah? Well, if that's what you want, I suppose it can't be helped. Let's pick up where we left off yesterday, then.”

lines.japanese: 「昨日って何ですか？」
lines.english: “What were we talking about yesterday?”

lines.japanese: 「シャッフルの話だ」
lines.english: “SHUFFLE!”

lines.japanese: 「ん、何か面白そうな話してる？」
lines.english: “Hm? Talking about something interesting?”

lines.japanese: さっきまで背を向けていた山科さんが、体をくるんと半回転させるのが見えた。
lines.english: Yamashina, who had been facing away from us, spun halfway around in her chair.

lines.japanese: 「よっ」
lines.english: “Yo.”

lines.japanese: 割と軽いフットワークで自分の席から離れると、山科さんは僕たちの食卓に加わってきた。
lines.english: She slipped out of her seat and joined us at our table.

lines.japanese: 「なあ羽田、おまえはゲームの深い部分がどうとか言っていたが、ギャルゲーとエロゲーではどっちが深い。おまえはそれを知っているのか」
lines.english: “Haneda, you were talking about the depths of games. Which goes deeper, dating games or adult games? Do you know?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは山科さんの存在に関心を示さず話の続きを投げかけてきた。彼女の方には顔すら向けようとしない。
lines.english: Hariu continued his question without showing the slightest interest in Yamashina's arrival. He did not even turn his face toward her.

lines.japanese: ただ、僕はそれどころじゃなかった。山科さんが今の話を聞いてチラリとこっちに目を向けたからだ。
lines.english: I had more immediate problems. Yamashina had heard the question and was shooting me a sidelong glance.

lines.japanese: 「は、針生さん、他にも面白いゲームはありますよ。そっちの話をしましょう」
lines.english: “H-Hariu, there are plenty of other interesting games. Let's talk about one of those.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、ネトゲの方が面白いよね」
lines.english: “Exactly. Online games are more fun, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん、ネトゲ。それもいいけど、今は男同士の話してるんだよ。自分の席にお帰り」
lines.english: “Online games, huh? That's fine, but the men are talking now. Run along to your own seat.”

lines.japanese: ようやく針生さんの目が山科さんの方に向いたかと思ったら、親指でくいと席に戻れという合図をした。僕は三人で話せばいいと思うんだけど……。
lines.english: When Hariu finally looked Yamashina's way, it was only to jerk his thumb toward her desk. I didn't see why the three of us couldn't talk together...

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、最近ちゃんと現実離れしてる？　さぼり癖ついてるんじゃないかな、駄目だよ現実逃避逃避は」
lines.english: “Haneda, have you been getting away from reality like you should? You haven’t started slacking, have you? No escaping from escapism.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは針生さんの声を無視して、僕に話を振ってきた。針生さんが目を細めつつ眼鏡のブリッジを指で上げる。
lines.english: Ignoring Hariu, Yamashina addressed me instead. Hariu narrowed his eyes and pushed up the bridge of his glasses with one finger.

lines.japanese: そういえば山科さんとオフで会って以来、そっちの世界にも行ってないなあ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I hadn't visited that world since meeting Yamashina offline.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと時間の都合とか、最近は色々ね」
lines.english: “I've been a little short on time. And, well... various things lately.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、充実してるんだね」
lines.english: “Hee hee. Sounds like your real life is pretty full.”

lines.japanese: 机の上に置いた袋をかさかさと開いて、山科さんも昼食を取りだした。彼女のメニューもパン食だった。
lines.english: Yamashina rustled open the bag on the desk and took out her own lunch. She was having bread too.

lines.japanese: ていうか、どこかで見たことあるサンドイッチだと思ったら、針生さんのと同じじゃないか。花水木通りのパン屋さんだ。
lines.english: In fact, I knew I had seen that sandwich somewhere. It was the same kind Hariu had—from the bakery on Hanamizuki Street.

lines.japanese: かり……と端っこを齧る山科さんが、小動物みたいでかわいい。
lines.english: Yamashina nibbled daintily at one corner. She looked as cute as a little animal.

lines.japanese: 彼女はツナと野菜が中心のサンドイッチだった。あのパンはプレーンな味わいだから、それにツナを挟んだらおいしいに違いない。やっぱりちょっとうらやましかった。
lines.english: Hers was mostly tuna and vegetables. The bread had such a plain, clean flavor that tuna was bound to suit it perfectly. Once again, I was a little jealous.

lines.japanese: 僕はなんだか、学食で買った自分のカツサンドが劣っているように思えて、残り半分を一気に口の中に突っこんだ。
lines.english: For some reason, my cafeteria cutlet sandwich suddenly seemed inferior. I stuffed the remaining half into my mouth all at once.

lines.japanese: 「いいな、私なんか、昨日も夜中急に寂しくなって、ずっとオンラインに閉じこもってたよ。もうほんと、食事とお風呂以外の時間は、部屋にひきこもりっきりで」
lines.english: “Must be nice. I suddenly got lonely again last night, so I spent the whole night shut away online. I hardly came out of my room except to eat and bathe.”

lines.japanese: 「部屋の中にいても生活音に苛まれる時があるし、家の外は尚更だし、こんな世の中じゃゲームの世界に逃げたくもなるよね」
lines.english: “Even in my room, the sounds of other people living their lives can torment me, and outside the house it's worse. In a world like this, of course you want to escape into a game.”

lines.japanese: 話の内容とは対照的に、山科さんは髪をさらさらと揺らしながら上品に笑った。
lines.english: In striking contrast to what she was saying, Yamashina laughed with perfect elegance, her silken hair swaying.

lines.japanese: 「分かる分かる」
lines.english: “I know exactly what you mean.”

lines.japanese: 言いながら、僕は中身のなくなったカツサンドの袋を見る。これだって僕はもっとゆっくり食べたかったのかもしれない。だけど味わうより先に逃げることを選んだんだ。
lines.english: As I spoke, I stared at the empty wrapper of my cutlet sandwich. Maybe I had wanted to eat it more slowly too. But I had chosen escape over taking the time to enjoy it.

lines.japanese: 「逃げたくなるよね」
lines.english: “It does make you want to run away.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんと二人で俯きあい、もそもそと昼食を口にする。そんな僕たちを眺めながら、針生さんはミネラルウォーターをごくりと飲みこんだ。
lines.english: Yamashina and I sat with our heads bowed, quietly working at our lunches. Hariu watched us and swallowed a mouthful of mineral water.

lines.japanese: 「それで現実逃避か」
lines.english: “And so you escape reality.”

lines.japanese: 「ち、違いますよ」
lines.english: “Th-that's not it.”

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて顔を上げた。
lines.english: I jerked up my head.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: だけど僕の視線の先に相手の目はなかった。針生さんの三白眼は相変わらず視点を定めずに、どこかをふらふらと泳いでいる。
lines.english: But his eyes were not there to meet mine. With slivers of white showing beneath the irises, Hariu's eyes kept wandering, never settling anywhere.

lines.japanese: 「妄想の世界に閉じこもる、俺はそれを逃げだとは思わないがなァ」
lines.english: “I don’t consider shutting yourself away inside a world of delusion to be an escape.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、どういうことですか」
lines.english: “Huh? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「それは……」
lines.english: “What I mean is...”

lines.japanese: 口を開きかけた針生さんは、泳がせていた視点をとめて急に考えこんだ。
lines.english: Hariu opened his mouth to answer, then stopped his wandering gaze and abruptly sank into thought.

lines.japanese: 「いや、やめとく。そういや明日香の受け売りだコレ。パクッたなんて思われたくねえや」
lines.english: “No, forget it. Come to think of it, that was me parroting Asuka. I don’t want anyone thinking I ripped it off.”

lines.japanese: え、渡来さんの受け売りって、彼女はなんて言ったんだろう。
lines.english: Something Watarai had said? I wondered what her words had been.

lines.japanese: 僕は針生さんの視線の先に渡来さんがいるのかと思って、首は動かないように横目で確認してみた。だけど、そこには空の机があるだけだった。
lines.english: I thought Watarai might be somewhere in the direction of Hariu's gaze, so I checked out of the corner of my eye without moving my head. There was only an empty desk.

lines.japanese: 針生さんに聞いてみようかと思ったけど、もう彼はパンを口に挟んでしまったから、話はそこで終わってしまった。
lines.english: I considered asking Hariu, but he had already clamped the sandwich between his teeth, and there the conversation ended.

lines.japanese: 僕は仕方なくうぐいすパンの袋をもそもそと開いた。
lines.english: With nothing else to do, I rustled open the wrapper of my sweet pea-paste bun.

lines.japanese: 「ところでさっきから気になってたんだけど、そのパン、おもしろそうだなァ」
lines.english: “By the way, I've been wondering about that bun. Looks interesting.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 僕は思わず袋から出そうとしていた手を止めた。このパン？　この、いたって普通のうぐいすパン？
lines.english: My hand stopped halfway into the wrapper. This bun? This perfectly ordinary sweet pea-paste bun?

lines.japanese: 「だってこれ、学食で買ったパンですよ」
lines.english: “But I bought it at the cafeteria.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど。日常の中に転がる石も、角度次第でダイヤに見えるってことか。おまえ、なかなかいいこと言うね」
lines.english: “I see. So even a stone lying in the road of everyday life can look like a diamond from the right angle. That's pretty profound, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 僕は何故か誉められていた。
lines.english: For some reason, he was praising me.

lines.japanese: 「あでも、実は私も思ってた。ちょっと欲しいなって」
lines.english: “Oh, but actually, I was thinking the same thing. I kind of want it too.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなの？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: そんなにおいしそうなパンを食べてるのに、この安っぽいうぐいすパンの方を選びたくなるときもあるんだろうか。不思議なこともあるもんだ。
lines.english: She had such a delicious-looking sandwich, yet apparently there were times when even she would rather have a cheap sweet pea-paste bun. Life was full of mysteries.

lines.japanese: 「なあ羽田、俺のパンやるから、おまえのソレ譲ってくんねえ？」
lines.english: “Haneda, I'll give you my sandwich. How about trading me that bun?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 僕からすれば好条件だ。花水木通りのパンの味が口の中にふわっと広がる。
lines.english: From my perspective, those were excellent terms. I could already imagine the flavor of the Hanamizuki Street bread spreading softly through my mouth.

lines.japanese: 「いいんですか？　こんな普通のパンでよければ、もちろん交換しますよ」
lines.english: “Are you sure? If you're happy with an ordinary bun like this, I'd be delighted to trade.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ずるい。それなら私のじゃ駄目かな」
lines.english: “Oh, that's not fair. Why not trade for mine instead?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんにパンを差しだそうとしたら、横から山科さんの右手が伸びてきた。その手で僕に待ったをかける。
lines.english: Just as I was about to hand the bun to Hariu, Yamashina's right hand shot in from the side and signaled me to stop.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめん、針生さんと約束しちゃったあとだし」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. I already promised it to Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 「まったくだよ、ひとの話に横から割りこんでくるとァどういうことだ。大人しくツナサンドでもかりかり齧ってなよ」
lines.english: “Exactly. What kind of person barges into somebody else’s negotiation? Go back to your tuna sandwich and nibble quietly.”

lines.japanese: 「決めるのは羽田君だもん」
lines.english: “Haneda gets to decide.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そんなこと言われても困るけど、確かに僕が何らかの決着をつけないと、場が収まりそうになかった。
lines.english: I wished she hadn't said that, but the situation plainly would not settle down until I brought it to some kind of conclusion.

lines.japanese: どうしよう。決断を迫られるというのは、すごく大変なことだといま知った。
lines.english: What was I going to do? Only now did I understand what a terrible burden it was to be forced into a decision.

lines.japanese: 「私、羽田君は裏切らないって信じてるから」
lines.english: “I believe Haneda would never betray me.”

lines.japanese: 「おい、この女引っぱたいていいか」
lines.english: “Hey. Mind if I slap this woman?”

lines.japanese: 「だ、駄目ですよ針生さん、女の子に暴力なんていけません」
lines.english: “N-no, Hariu. You can't hit a girl.”

lines.japanese: 「私は暴力には屈しない」
lines.english: “I will not submit to violence.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな大げさな話じゃないよ」
lines.english: “This isn't anything that dramatic.”

lines.japanese: 「叩きたければ叩け、その代わり惨めになるのは自分だ」
lines.english: “Strike me if you wish. You’ll only make yourself look pathetic.”

lines.japanese: 「もう、仲良くしてよ二人とも」
lines.english: “Come on, both of you. Please try to get along.”

lines.japanese: 「だったらどっちと交換するか早く選べ」
lines.english: “Then hurry up and decide which of us you're trading with.”

lines.japanese: 「ほらこのキュウリのサンドイッチうまいぞ。交換だ交換」
lines.english: “Here. This cucumber sandwich is good. Let's trade.”

lines.japanese: 「キュウリ……」
lines.english: “Cucumber...”

lines.japanese: それなら針生さんには申し訳ないけど考える余地はない。僕はキュウリが苦手だった。
lines.english: In that case, I was sorry for Hariu, but there was nothing to consider. I hated cucumber.

lines.japanese: 「あの、すみません。やっぱりおれは山科さんの……」
lines.english: “Um, sorry. I think I'd rather have Yamashina's...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、やっぱり私？　このトマトサンドイッチおいしいんだよ」
lines.english: “Oh! Mine after all? This tomato sandwich is delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、やっぱりみんなで半分こしましょう」
lines.english: “Um... Why don't the three of us split everything?”

lines.japanese: 僕はトマトも嫌いだった。仕方ないので、みんなが半分こずつ交換する流れになった。
lines.english: I hated tomatoes too. With no other way out, we ended up splitting everything and trading halves.

lines.japanese: キュウリとトマトのサンドイッチは、やっぱり青臭くて好きになれない。だけど、僕のうぐいすパンを半分ずつ食べた二人は満足していたので、結果オーライだ。
lines.english: The cucumber and tomato sandwiches had exactly the grassy taste I disliked. But the other two were pleased with their halves of my sweet pea-paste bun, so it all worked out.

lines.japanese: そのあと二人が買ったパン屋さんの店長夫婦の話になった。特に盛りあがりもなかったけど、昼休みの終わりまで三人で過ごした。
lines.english: After that, we got to talking about the husband and wife who ran the bakery. It was hardly a thrilling conversation, but the three of us stayed together until lunch ended.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんもいれば誘いたいと思ったけど、残念なことに彼女は昼休みの時間中、教室に帰ってこなかった。
lines.english: If Watarai had been there, I would have invited her too. Unfortunately, she did not return to the classroom at any point during lunch.

lines.japanese: 予鈴のベルが鳴ったので、僕はトイレに行っておこうと思い席から離れた。
lines.english: The warning bell rang. Thinking I ought to visit the restroom, I left my seat.

lines.japanese: 教室の後ろのドアへ向かう途中、バスケ部の鴻野君たちの話し声が聞こえた。
lines.english: On my way to the rear door, I heard Kono and the other boys from the basketball club talking.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、アイツらってあーいうキャラだっけ？」
lines.english: “Were those guys always like that?”

lines.japanese: 「なんか楽しそーじゃねえ？　そういや毎日残ってるみたいだしな」
lines.english: “Looks like they're having fun, doesn't it? Come to think of it, they've been staying late every day.”

lines.japanese: もしかして僕たちのことを言ってるのかなと思ったけど、僕はトイレに向かうところだったから、声はかけられなかった。
lines.english: I wondered if they meant us, but I was on my way to the restroom and couldn't stop to speak to them.

lines.japanese: あ、渡来さん……。
lines.english: Oh. Watarai...

lines.japanese: 廊下に出ると、渡来さんが教室に戻るところだった。
lines.english: When I stepped into the corridor, Watarai was on her way back to the classroom.

lines.japanese: 体調のことを聞こうかと思ったけど、彼女はすぐに教室に入ってしまった。
lines.english: I thought about asking how she felt, but she slipped inside before I could.

lines.japanese: 残念だけどまた帰り際にでも声をかけてみよう。僕はトイレへと急いで向かった。
lines.english: Too bad. I would try speaking to her on the way home instead. I hurried off toward the restroom.
